title: Ethiopian Avocado Salad
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Avocado Salad — ripe avocado sliced and dressed with lemon, jalapeño, onion, and fresh coriander. Ethiopia grows excellent avocados in its highland areas, and this simple salad celebrates the fruit at its best.
longDesc: Ethiopia is one of Africa's major avocado producers — the highland areas produce buttery, rich avocados of outstanding quality. This simple salad showcases them with the most minimal dressing.
ingredients: ½ red onion — very thinly sliced
steps: Arrange avocado slices on a plate.
Scatter thinly sliced onion and jalapeño.
Dress with lemon juice and oil.
chefTips: Ripe avocados only — they should yield to gentle pressure.
cookingScience: Avocado browns through enzymatic oxidation — the enzyme polyphenol oxidase reacts with phenolic compounds in the presence of oxygen. Lemon juice's citric acid inhibits polyphenol oxidase activity, slowing browning for 30—60 minutes.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland avocados — grown in the same systems as coffee.
healthBenefits: Very high in healthy monounsaturated fats.
culturalNote: Ethiopian avocado salad represents the modern Ethiopian café culture — the same avocados that have been grown in the highlands for generations, now served in the contemporary format that young Ethiopians enjoy.
